The Table 2 current-case row and the narrative use different reference points, so they are recorded as ambiguities, not conflicts: the row gives 4 years between the last travel to a tropical/subtropical country and disease onset, while the text gives the last trip to Mali in 2013 and the referral in 2018; the row gives a follow-up of 12 months, while the text gives remission 18 months after the surgery and 12 months after stopping antifungal therapy. The row lists three treatment lines (surgery; terbinafine and posaconazole for 5 months; surgery with posaconazole for 3 months, followed by relapse) and omits the final wide excision with voriconazole described in the text.

The Figure 4B caption states MRI-confirmed complete remission at six months follow-up without naming the treatment the follow-up starts from; the text describes two excisions followed by antifungal therapy (the posaconazole course was followed by a recurrence one year after it stopped) and reports remission 18 months after the final surgery.
The abstract places the first nodule on the dominant hand’s ring finger, while the case text places it on the fourth finger of the right hand; handedness is not stated.
